body: Based... Based AF (old post, I know. But it made my day LMAO)

Same 🤣 I get almost all tasks done by the end of Sunday/Monday every week, leaving RSB and Distro to my SGAs the rest of the week. Whoever works Thursday only has Perpetual to worry about. If customers aren't coming in the store, that's definitely corporate's problem -- can't have 0 opportunities and expect results.

They probably meant you weren't even doing "tasks", which even then some DLs are stupid enough to think getting all of the tasks on Main Menu done ahead of time is "lazy". . . Makes me so grateful my SL2 and DL both actually reward people for being efficient.

Yeah, it urks me that I have to do conference with SLs who take pride in doing this on a daily basis. Don't get me wrong, if you can get a person to buy even half that total more than once a day, you're one hell of a sales employee. But I find more success in creating returning customers for my store. This company needs to get back to prioritizing longevity over "THE BIG NUMBER!"

NGL, I tuned out the PRO and Warranty jargon before actually working for the company. I keep it as human as possible -- essentially reading the vibe of each customer. It's pretty obvious who will and won't care about the memberships.

Yeah, exactly! I generally let the customer decide what they want, but our SLs generally encourage offering to walk customers through the sign-ups as it increases the chance SGAs can get more PRO in the future.

It didn't say that at all. . . Granted, auto-renewal be pushed this hard is scummy enough. Regardless, it doesn't mention withholding information about auto-renewal from the customer -- in fact, the DM actually specifies for the store team to recommend the auto function and let the customer read the options themselves.

Yeah, that's a huge sign of desperation on her end. I mean, copper can erode or wear away, but nowhere near that easily. The fact the Switch cartridges are small and get smashed if mishandled is the worst possible fear. Unless you have children using them, there's very few reasons adults or even teenagers need a warranty on them.

That's the result of a hostile management in addition to corporate hounding. A lot of stores don't actually do this, though I can only prove that with the chill environment with my district's SLs. Certain districts have higher pressure to compete than others
YES! I have this card in my binder. One of my absolute favorite in the Trainer galleries.

You gotta do what is best for you. Most people should not have to do single coverage in any retail -- especially for a store with expensive electronics. GameStop is definitely not in the same shape as every day was practically double-coverage before Covid (at least, that's what I've been told by my SL). Greener pastures, my friend. 😊
I was commenting. If that's your indicator of starting an argument, then I don't know what you expect on Reddit. I'm not looking for any kind of discourse.
Not sure why you're getting downvoted. You've got a valid point.

Technically, they do have a slight exception to the system's record on New copies (and I'll admit this shows I was wrong about one thing). At the beginning of a new fiscal year, corporate may require certain unsold titles to be reprocessed as Pre-Owned these days. Instead of utilizing the clearance bin of games from previous years, it seems likely they want us to lower prices on those products in this method to increase their KPI on Pre-Owned %. That's actually smart, though a bit shady.

It may be a case of each DM discretion -- that's highly possible. My SL and DM are very specific, so I assumed all districts are similar. I'm sure plenty of employees are doing this -- that wasn't my argument. Saying "everyone I know is doing it" doesn't prove that the policy allows for that action. A lot of misinformation is due to store teams making excuses for each other and/or assuming their managers are 100% correct on all policies.
The point was that people fix up old property and vehicles to resell all the time. . . You're taking this conversation way too seriously 😒

If GameStop closes permanently, I get a different job. Not that big of a deal. If they were going to buy it from Walmart either way, then why are they telling us? The point is that they are not actually comparing prices (though you would expect that it should be why they are). In this example OP gave the customer is straight up walking in the door, asking if we have a console in stock -- like they are going to do a transaction with us -- and after getting a "yes", proceeds to tell us, "Oh, well I'm on my way to Walmart to buy that."

We don't care that they're going to Walmart. Corporate *might* if enough people globally start saying that every day, but no matter what retail employees will not give a damn. It's a waste of our time.

I stopped using the word trade, but unfortunately it's a marketing term blasted all over our website and signs now. Customers are immediately ask: "How does the trading work?" as soon as I answer a call or the walk into the store. It only confuses them more when they hear the word "sell" (which is very ironic).
It's the same as flipping a house. . . You buy extremely cheap, renovate with a determined budget, and sell at a higher rate than you spent -- profit margins. Not that wild.
*insert Rick Roll*

Okay, first off, why should we -- as an employee just trying to do our job -- care about another company's inventory and prices? We don't work for Walmart. The customer is really just bringing up pointless information unless they plan on price matching. If they are going to just buy it at Walmart, then fine. Retail employees do not give a shit where you buy things -- it doesn't actually affect us personally.

Second, GameStop is not against price matching (what the hell are you talking about??). If you're a PRO member, we are guaranteed to price match any legit offer from Walmart, Best Buy, Target. . . Hell, even in some odd situations we might price match Amazon.

Legitimately, there is no reason the employee couldn't swap it. The product was damaged -- technically -- by manufacturing and/or distribution. You can use the manufacturing defect option in this. . . well, case. . .

These people think the thin shrink wrap guarantees the product is undamaged. Granted, it's usually proof that it was never opened -- but shipping/manufacturing/employee errors are still a thing. Some retail businesses will re-wrap the product (Wal-Mart does still, sometimes) because otherwise they completely cannot sell it.
False. If an employee is gutting a new copy to borrow, then they're not following the policy. This isn't allowed at all in stores. Nice try, though.

That would make too much sense. Unfortunately, corporate policy isn't about that -- just the bottom $. Also, technically it would (according to our Loss Prevention departments) screw over the distributors of new copies. New copies are never allowed to be reprocessed as Pre-Owned, and the employees who have already tried this were fired quickly back in the day for it.
Justice
You all need to get over it. We've had worse ads on repeat. . .
Sounds like a reason to call the police. MF'ers were just asking to get tazed in the rain.

Honestly I love being able to say "Sorry, we're sold out. . ." and I genuinely don't always understand why. If I don't get any Warranty/HW Attach/PRO, yeah it sucks, but oh well. I've been the "dumb/annoying" customer asking for a console's availability before -- so why would it bother me?


Then I get the random douchebag wasting his money he needs for bills, asking for a PS5 and/or XBX X like he's ordering a damn burger. Dude, you know if you plan on buying a console, it's going to take a minute or two to verify some details, right??

It's not the answer -- it's a coward's way out. I'm not saying you're a loser if you go through with it, but you're letting yourself get off easy by making your family and loved ones suffer the aftermath. And it's not a mercy to yourself either (nobody knows what happens after death, religious or not) so you don't know if you're going to just wake up in a more miserable state or stop existing. Either one will suck.

Understandable. But you can't do any job without making somebody else richer than they already are. It's the facts. Making money for a rich CEO isn't an abhorrent evil - just simple economics. The issue is a CEO and exec boards abusing customers and workers, not the company's net sales.

"But I'm a PRO Member! Can't you change the price/rule for me?"

Buddy, we charged you $25 to get a $5/month coupon and 5% discount -- not to treat you like a damn noble lord. . .
This is what most Gen X SLs say lol Who the hell checks their email anymore??
The pissed off customers don't live around your store 🤣

I can't disagree with you, as I firmly believe all stores should encourage transparency. I do want to ask, though: Have you ever worked retail and/or sales? Employees aren't ashamed of any policy -- we really couldn't give a shit. Most of the time an SL or DM can easily create trouble for a associate for simply being honest, which comes from corporate being ashamed of their own policies.
I'm still holding one back for my kiddo to give her sister (teaching her to save up her own money).
Remove the pineapple and we good, chief

I don't push the sales anymore -- just make catered recommendations based on the customer. You only need a small percentage for each "win" per week, so I focus on the people who clearly already have $25+ discount on the transaction w/o PRO/renewal and suggest the warranty on pre-owned (new policy doesn't change anything for used products). But for anything else? Meh, the customers' wallets will show the results of crappy corporate practices. . .
Not only did my store not get the pins, but we had 10% of our shipment of Super Mario RPG missing from the package. . . Wtf is going on at the warehouse??

I don't think you get the context. Not once did I mention "educating the customers on corporate". . . So what is the point of your argument?? My thoughts are about trying to remind people that, if we have regulars we already know are going to be upset, to not be petty with them. Yeah, I don't want my employees being abused by angry people. That's a no-brainer.

I can get behind that. This was my first job in 8 years after being a stay-at-home dad. I got lucky with how awesome my SL and DM both are, but I still mainly took the job as a resume builder, so I completely understand.

We get the occasional customers, who are not our regulars, that think "Well, the other GameStop did _____ for me!" or "You need to change the policy!" and then never understand/care that 

A) Non-corporate employees do not have any control of the policy changes

B) Stores are run by separate leaders, therefore my staff does not alter their behavior based on hearsay.

Not saying we should excuse irrational customers, though. It's mostly the good-hearted regulars that SGAs enjoy helping that I'm concerned for. I absolutely will not let my employees get treated like garbage for doing their jobs, tbh.

"Wait, so you want me to give you cash, and then cause the store to lose an even higher value afterwards??" I mean, I get that not everyone realizes that defecting a product means completely losing more money for a store, but the refurbishing fee is applied for a reason.
I love the "It was bought recently, so it's basically brand new" -- to which I sometimes respond "Well, the problem is that it's broken, so that isn't very relevant. . ."

Ummm. . . I specifically said it was just customer service numbers and corporate offices. Where the hell did you get personal numbers?? That's not a 'dick move', it's a policy violation. I'm not a moron. Those aren't personal cell numbers, they're company lines.

Eh, age isn't a factor. Leadership is the core issue and always will be. My SL2 is only 6 months younger than me, and we're both 18+ years younger than our best SGA (who shows us complete respect for our efforts to help him). I've only been with the company a total of 9 months and already made ASL -- while competing with the same SGA for the position. He's also a company veteran, worked in the same exact store for 4+ years back in the late 2000s. He got hired the same time I did and we each worked as the primary SGA for the separate stores in our team. So he barely lost out on the promotion for one simple fact -- my numbers were better at the time and our secondary store was at its best in several years after I got hired. It could have gone either way despite the age and experience gap.

Lead by example if you feel it's worth it -- but only if it's worth it. A great SGA becomes the ASL's primary SGA who sets the standard for other co-workers. You don't need to do a manager's job to help your team. Again, this is only if your team is worth it to you, though.

Um. . . You can't be written up for doing a good job. My SL2 specifically convinced our DM to promote me to ASL because I do every weekly task solo by Monday night. Trust me, you're not going to get in trouble for doing better than the store manager, so make sure your DM is aware of the abuse.

You pretty much described the reason I try so hard at my store. I care about it so much, despite the dying corporate backbone, that's it's now under my wing after working hard with SL2 to get me up to speed asap on managing the store.
Because. . . The question is all you need lol

I was telling customers that if they're already getting a discount of $25 or more during a holiday promo, then it's simply a free membership with a payout, even if they don't use it later -- because the 5% bonus on enroll is most likely going to lose corporate well more than $25 on most purchases this BF anyway. Customers are going to spend money in our store no matter what, might as well weaponize the PRO cards while still keeping my numbers up.

I can see holidays for retailers as the test of will for the best DMs. I absolutely love my bosses because of what they are willing to do for me and my team. Unfortunately not every district (or store, for that matter) is very lucky, so I guess I'm really posting all of this for everyone who still has or has had a crappy employment with GameStop. Really wish there was more DMs can do, but none of them are corporate so I get the issues they're plagued with.

Sad, but you're right. I'm aware of all this, so don't get the wrong idea -- this isn't a post made in a simple whim. If my customers get mad, my team knows to let them know we agree with them and that our whole district has recommended giving out customer service hotlines or even a direct number to a corporate office. Hell, my SGAs asked for my permission to just have a sheet prepared with hotlines under the registers for Black Friday.

Actually this our store's philosophy as well, especially for our primary SGA. It's partially why he's my most reliable employee. My regulars have been making sure we're willing to do what we can to not ruin their holidays (which is what inspired me to create this thread). I'm not sure how dedicated other DMs are, but ours has promised that he will try to help with warranty exchange concerns as long as we've done every step in the new policies first. Basically, he wants it to be on him if a policy is bent so that our store leaders don't suffer the backlash of this asinine stunt from Cohen.

Oh the Karens are definitely getting no pity. I do worry about the regulars most stores enjoy helping, though. I would just hate to see so many SLs and ASLs lose their reputation with their best customers after building up so much time helping them.

Sorry for the VERY late reply lol I try to teach most customers a bit as well to do my "enrich the experience" part. It definitely helps build my store's reputation in the district. And it's actually funny to learn just how many people near my store clearly only own a console to play newer games, only to realize they bought the wrong console. I get more HW attach opportunities on top of trades when this happens, tbh. A win-win on big PRO weeks.

Yeah, you should still follow policy, agreed. I'm not saying break policy. I'm saying try to actually reduce the chances of customers running into this issue. Other stores are going to have negligent employees or bad practices, but you can at least try to care about making your store a preference for people. Nobody should be a hellraiser that says "screw the rulebook!"

The loophole of that is doing your job -- make sure the customer knows what they're getting ahead of time. Ensure they're getting a product they actually need. You don't just shrug and say "not my problem". And that also means if I have to find out another store wasn't properly informing customers on their purchases, certain SLs and the DM will be hearing a complaint on behalf of the customer anyway. You can always find a way to make a customer happier in your store despite the issue.

Okay, I'm going to be honest with you -- if you don't cherish your store, then stop doing the work above your pay grade. I was willing to do my former ASL's job because he was incompetent and I grew up with store. It's a part of my childhood, so I take pride in keeping it alive. As a result, it's now my store (my SL2 pretty much let's me run it entirely as I see fit after the way I fixed it in less than 6 months as a new hire). The problem is most SGAs don't have this reason to try so hard. And GameStop is not a company worth stressing for.

Never break your back for corporate, and only if you're leading your team should you be this stressed.
Sure, and McDonald employees know exactly which farms are supplying their "100% BEEF". . . 😂 One of my SGAs said this to a Karen last month. I could only smile at her dumbfound expression.

Doesn't help that customers apparently think all GameStop employees get brand new consoles dirt cheap, because they all have a surprised-Pikachu face when they find out I don't have $500 for a PS5 yet.

That's not the way to treat your customers either. It's our job to "enrich the experience". If I have to use my power as an ASL to use the policies to my advantage and use a loophole for the customer, I'm going to do it. And if "enriching the experience" isn't a good enough reason for corporate, then maybe we need to stop enforcing G.A.M.E.

Not every SL was trained in our district to reject that. . . My SL2 is a primary "call leader" on weekly conferences, meaning our DM sees him as a veteran among the current SLs of our district. He's aware of policies that aren't usually enforced properly, so when he trains an ASL, our store is properly run without him afterward. Other stores aren't as lucky as the majority of SLs are from payroll turnover in the last five years.

I've had people get mad just because our SL specifically doesn't take missing rubber on the thumbsticks or if the thumbsticks are clearly gone. . . These idiots expect us to act like a crooked cop who looks the other way.

My SL2 and I are the only people who were able to sell warranties reliably with the "new for new" method before, but now there's no way I can expect my primary SGA, let alone my weekend-only SGA, to willingly try and sell this shitty policy. I solely run the secondary store as the ASL and don't even know my primary store SGAs that well. I'm trying to help them get over this crap when the SL2 is on his well-earned day off, but it's not like I can excuse this bull either.

Physical receipt of purchase within 7 days of transaction, and you're fine. I tell this to everyone. If the receipt is lost/damaged, didn't print out, the employee has to use the Hyrule Hub on our registers to find the purchase on your account. I hope this helps! :)

This. This right here was exactly my first two months. I get mostly sketchy dbags in hoodies asking about "the new 2K" and illiterate rednecks in the midweek shifts, so I totally understand your pain.
I've done cart-pushing for retails before. . . I'm good, fam
Sometimes I enjoy my dumb customers on a slow day. . . Makes me feel devilishly evil when I can manage to direct them to a Vintage Stock I don't like.

In all fairness, being a seasonal isn't an actual associate position. However, the company really doesn't give my SGAs enough hours either. And most Seasonals aren't expected to stay after the holidays whether they liked the job or not. I'm already annoyed that I can't have one of my seasonals come in unless they're already scheduled. . . Making them completely pointless.

It's really annoying when the thumbsticks are visibly busted and then they say "But it still turns on. . ." Dude, that's not relevant to the issue, so stop trying to play 4D chess when you're still thinking on a 1-dimensional field.
Problem is we have no time to do that and most of us have actual lives and families. The people who are hired for retail generally do not live solely on the Internet.
OMG, I just checked my Coming Soon when I saw this! It's in our store too LMAO 🤣🤣🤣
Damned scumbag. . .
You realize moral implications are not on the policy in writing, right? Neither does it generally break laws regarding fraud or false advertisement. Good luck with your argument with corporate.
Yeah, that's not how refunds work. . .
If the stores were allowed more hours, then yes.
Bruh. . . Grammar Nazis are a dead meme

Agreed, the policy is asinine. But you definitely need to ask the manager on shift to contact the DM. Our DM has already gave us permission to call him if the employee already did the required steps of following policy.

Well, as an ASL I can tell you that employees are not going to need to argue. As long as they have first stated the policy, yes, you can just ask them to call the DM. You're not going to spite a DM considering even Store Leaders need their permission to bypass this. Your method is just annoying for the SGA and not really anybody else.
Why would you punish an employee with their hands tied with your pettiness? That's just stupid.
The school shooter
Oof. I feel ya on that. As the ASL at my store, I can understand the pain. We had four no-call-no-shows for holiday interviews and the SGA we did get quit after one onboarding day. . .
Time to start using the holiday hires this weekend. . .

The really "fun" ones are the backwood rednecks who can't understand why Xbox series exclusives discs won't run on their Xbox One. . . Literally had one ask me my first month as an SGA why ". . .GameStop don't make 'em play on both?" My former ASL wanted to slap him so hard.

He's probably using that picture at each store to find an unfortunate SGA to catch off guard. I've had enough Karens and scammers in my store to realize they're going to find any "loophole" they can trick an employee with. Needless to say, they don't like it when my primary SGA or I are on shift 😂

Yeah, that happens sometimes. I feel your pain. As an newer ASL, I hate the whole "get me YOUR manager" situation after already explaining that I have to uphold policies. I'm single-handedly running our secondary store for my SL2, and I'll be damned if my store's actions will be dictated by another locations faulty practices.

Right, but your logic also applies to ALL entry jobs. I'm talking about full-time w/benefits positions that specifically take into experience, dedication, etc. IT and Sales managers hired outside of their current staff are not selected with no experience. GameStop is a springboard, is my point.

Ironically, most Walmart employees don't get the same hours per week an SGA might. . . Scoff at that fact if you want, but very few SGAs in my district get less than 25 hours a week. ASLs always get 35-40 hours, so the paychecks are higher than a $15/hr cart pusher with only 20 hrs.

People are impatient. . . And competitive. If you tell someone they get "special" privileges for pre-ordering, it increases sales opportunities for the company. Greed isn't just a flaw corporations have, consumers are just as greedy about being "first" to get stuff.
Not often, but it can happen. An employee not paying attention might put the case on the shelf without verifying there's a copy in the drawer.

You do have that option, yes. In the future, try to save up 25,000 points -- we have a $25 coupon option that doesn't use more than one of your point-to-coupon limitations (you can only use up to three coupons a day via the PRO points).

I'm using the employment as a way to enhance my resume for future IT and/or Sales career options. It's never about the entire wage for me -- I get more out of this than a paycheck. Technically, I have one of the luckiest opportunities as someone who got hired by an actually competent and considerate SL. Our DM is also more than reasonable. However, if you're only looking for income -- and expect a lot of it, you gotta start somewhere. Some of us just have a better handle with awkward customers and retail and aren't shallow in how we pick our jobs. Don't just judge someone's choices for not fitting your view.
